procnotices.notice_text:
AVISO GENERAL DE CONTRATACIÓN

 

 

ESTADO PLURINACIONAL DE BOLIVIA

PROYECTO DE PROTECCIÓN ECONÓMICA  Y TRANSFORMACIÓN SOCIAL

SECTOR PROTECCIÓN SOCIAL Y EMPLEO

ANUNCIO GENERAL DE ADQUISICIONES

Préstamo N° 9927-BO

Proyecto No. P514751

El Estado Plurinacional de Bolivia ha recibido un financiamiento por un monto equivalente a USD 200,501,255.00 (Doscientos millones quinientos un mil doscientos cincuenta y cinco 00/100 dólares de los Estados Unidos de Norteamérica) del Banco Mundial para el costo del Proyecto de Protección Económica y Transformación Social, y se propone utilizar parte de los fondos para efectuar pagos correspondientes a la adquisición de Bienes, Servicios de No-Consultoría y Servicios de Consultoría bajo este proyecto, que será ejecutado a través del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas Públicas (MEFP) como entidad responsable de la implementación del proyecto, a través de la Unidad de Ejecución del Proyecto (UEP).

El proyecto incluirá los siguientes componentes

Componente 1: Transferencias Monetarias (USD 192,000,000). Este componente financiará transferencias monetarias a beneficiarios seleccionados para brindar apoyo de ingresos a poblaciones vulnerables afectadas por choques económicos o climáticos. Las transferencias se canalizarán a través de: (i) el Programa Extraordinario para la Equidad y Protección (PEPE), de carácter temporal, destinado a hogares en situación de vulnerabilidad; y (ii) los Programas Sociales Existentes, incluyendo el Bono de Discapacidad, el Bono Juana Azurduy, el Bono Juancito Pinto, el Bono Anual de Indigencia y la Renta Dignidad

Componente 2: Fortalecimiento de los Sistemas de Prestación de Protección Social y Gestión del Proyecto (USD 8,000,000).  Este componente consta de dos partes:

Parte 2.1: Fortalecimiento de los Sistemas de Prestación de Protección Social (USD 7,500,000). Este componente financiará servicios de consultoría, servicios de no consultoría y bienes destinados a modernizar la infraestructura tecnológica e institucional del sistema de protección social boliviano. Las adquisiciones bajo este Sub-componente comprenden: (i) Servicios de Consultoría: contratación de firma para la gestión integral de los procesos de admisión, registro y atención de casos del Registro de Hogares y Registro Social; desarrollo de una plataforma para el relevamiento de información socioeconómica de hogares e individuos que soporte la Red de Protección Social; desarrollo y publicación de material promocional de la Red de Protección Social; servicios de auditoría financiera externa del proyecto; y contratación de consultores individuales especializados en sistemas informáticos, adquisiciones, gestión financiera, impacto social, seguridad de plataformas y monitoreo de la red, adscritos a la Unidad de  Ejecución del Proyecto (UEP).

Parte 2.2: Gestión del Proyecto (USD 500,001.86). Este componente financiará el apoyo a    la implementación del Componente 1 del Proyecto, incluyendo la contratación de personal especializado   , gestión de adquisiciones, gestión financiera,   actividades de monitoreo y evaluación, y costos operativos necesarios.

La adquisición de contratos financiados por el Banco Mundial se llevará a cabo mediante los procedimientos especificados en las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones para Prestatarios en Proyectos de Inversión, para Bienes, Obras, Servicios de No-Consultoría y Servicios de Consultoría de julio de 2016, revisadas en septiembre de 2025, y podrán participar todas las empresas y personas elegibles como se define en las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones. Después de las negociaciones del proyecto, el Banco Mundial publicará en su sitio web externo el plan de adquisición inicial acordado y todas las actualizaciones posteriores, una vez haya otorgado su no-objeción.

Los Avisos Específicos de Adquisiciones (AEA) para contratos sujetos a la competencia abierta se anunciarán, a medida que estén disponibles, en la página web externa del Banco Mundial y en la página oficial del Sistema de Contrataciones Estatales de Bolivia (www.sicoes.gob.bo) y/o periódicos de circulación nacional en el país.

Las empresas y personas elegibles interesadas que deseen ser consideradas para la provisión de bienes, servicios de no  consultoría y servicios de consultoría para el proyecto mencionado anteriormente, o quienes requieran información adicional, deben contactar con el Prestatario en la dirección siguiente:

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT)

 

Country: Ethiopia

Name of Project: The Building Institutions and Systems to Harness and Realize Agenda (BIASHARA) 2063 Project

Grant No: P180117

Assignment Title: Individual Consultant – Internal Auditor (IA)

Reference No. ET-AUC-549624-CS-INDV

 

The African Union Commission has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of The Building Institutions and Systems to Harness and Realize Agenda (BIASHARA) 2063 Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include providing objective assurance to the World Bank Group through the African Union Commission Office of Internal Oversight that: the governance processes, financial management and procurement processes comply with requirements; and that project procedures and internal controls are adequate and effective to mitigate current and emerging risks and fraud. Specific tasks include:

  • Identify the strategic, operational, financial as well as compliance risks and ensure adequate reporting so that the risks are well mitigated or well managed.
  • Conduct audits and investigate possible fraudulent behavior and communicate findings and recommend appropriate action to the Office of Internal Oversight Directorate and World Bank Group.
  • Assess the significance of the organization’s risks and the effectiveness of risk management efforts, communicate these to management and develop recommendations to improve risk management.
  • Conduct independent and objective assessments of the project’s operational, internal controls, and compliance process and ensure accuracy and transparency with established policies and procedures.
  • Evaluate internal control efficiency and effectiveness and provide management assurance that the controls in place are adequate to respond to the risks that threaten the projects. Also examine operations to determine whether they are efficient and effective
  • Ensure financial transactions’ accuracy and examine the reliability and integrity of financial and operational information.
  • Track implementation of audit recommendations, report unresolved control weaknesses;  and monitor corrective actions.
  • Evaluate the procedures used to safeguard project assets from theft, fire, illegal activities, or other types of loss and make recommendations for enhanced protection.
  • Prepare audit reports according to the procedures of the Office of Internal Oversight
  • Interact with all Office of Internal Oversight staff to inform the scope of the assignment to be embarked on, and report the outcomes to the Office Of Internal Oversight Directorate.
  • Carry out any other duties as may be assigned from time to time

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expression of Interest.

The African Union Commission now invites eligible individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

  • Academic qualifications and membership

 

  • Bachelor’s degree in auditing, finance, accounting, business, economics, or commerce.
  • A professional audit or accounting qualification (Certified Internal Auditor (CIA), Certified Public Accountant (CPA), Association of Certified Chartered Accountants (ACCA).
  • An active member (in good standing) of a professional body would be an added advantage

 

  • Work experience

 

  • At least eight (8) years of experience in auditing (internal or external), risk and financial management, with a proven record in conducting internal audits and ensuring regulatory compliance
  • Knowledge and experience of the World Bank's audit requirements will be a preference.
  • Preference will be given to candidates with experience in managing and/or auditing donor funded projects

 

  • Technical proficiency

 

  • Relevant knowledge of International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) and the International Standards on Auditing (ISAs).
  • Familiarity with auditing software tools, as well as solid understanding of accounting principles and project processes. Knowledge of Teammate plus audit software would be an added advantage
  • Demonstrated ability to learn new technology quickly and effectively use it for maximum productivity.

 

  • Ethical standards

 

  • Strong ethical foundation and integrity are vital for handling sensitive and confidential information appropriately.

 

  • Analytical skills

 

  • Ability to research, analyze and synthesize information, interpret data, retrieve information from computerized accounting systems, and to summarize results clearly and concisely.
  • Possess strong analytical and problem-solving skills to identify issues and inefficiencies within financial records and operational processes.
  • Results-oriented personality with proven problem-solving skills, strong quantitative skills and attention to detail.

 

  • Communication and interpersonal skills
  • Strong communication skills with ability to prepare presentations and discuss findings in written and oral form.
  • Capacity to function as a member of a diverse and multi-disciplinary team.
  • Proficiency in English. A working knowledge of other AU official or working language (s) is an added advantage.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016, revised November 2020 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant selection method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours i.e. 0900 to 1700 hours.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by e-mail) by 06 August 2026

 

African Union Commission,

Building C, 3rd Floor,

P.O Box 3243, Roosevelt Street

Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

Tel: +251 (0) 11 551 7700 – Ext 4305

  1. Duty Station

The selected candidates shall be based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia at the African Union Headquarters.

  1. Contract Duration

  1. Renumeration

procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

 

 

National Recovery Program Bureau (NRPB)

 

Consulting services for feasibility assessment, detailed design, procurement support, and construction supervision for the development of the VROMI Waste Diversion and Waste Management Yard

 

 

Country: Sint Maarten

Project: The Sint Maarten Emergency Debris Management Project

Assignment Title: Consulting Services for Land Survey and Planning

Credit/Loan no.: TF-B9747

Reference no.: SX-NRPB-556005-CS-CQS

 

Deadline: 5:00 p.m. Atlantic Standard Time, Monday, August 10th, 2026

 

1. The Government of Sint Maarten (GoSXM) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Emergency Debris Management Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services under this request for expression of interest.

2. The Government of Sint Maarten (GoSXM), represented by the National Recovery Program Bureau (NRPB) is looking to select an experienced (international or national) firm for a consultancy service to conduct the feasibility assessment, detailed design, procurement support, and construction supervision services. The objective of this consultancy is to provide multidisciplinary engineering and technical services to assess the feasibility of developing the VROMI Waste Diversion and Waste Management Yard, prepare the detailed designs and procurement documents, and supervise the implementation of the civil works.

3. The scope of services under this consultancy includes, but is not limited to, the following:

a. Conduct land assessment activities, including boundary surveys, geotechnical investigations, soil bearing capacity and groundwater analysis, utilities assessment, and environmental, social, health and safety (ESHS) screening;

b. Prepare a master site development plan, detailed engineering designs, cadastral subdivision plans, and technical documentation to support regulatory approvals;

c. Develop procurement documentation for the civil works, including technical specifications, Bills of Quantities (BoQ), engineer's estimates, and provide technical support during the procurement and bid evaluation process;

d. Provide construction supervision services, including quality assurance, contract administration, ESHS monitoring, and reporting throughout the implementation of the works.

e. The detailed scope of services and deliverables is provided in the attached Terms of Reference (TOR). The assignment will be implemented in three phases:

Phase 1 – Land Assessment and Preparation;

Phase 2 – Planning, Detailed Design and Procurement Support;

Phase 3 – Construction Supervision (optional, subject to implementation of the civil works contract).

4. The detailed scope and deliverables of the assignment are available in Terms of Reference (TOR), which can be viewed and downloaded via the link: National Recovery Program Bureau of St. Maarten - Consulting Services for Land Survey and Planning. The consulting services are to be provided over an estimated 5 months; this assignment will be on a lump-sum basis (firm fixed price) for all services and expenses, including consultant travel expenses.

5. The Consultant shall ensure that all activities are implemented in accordance with the quality standards, time and budget elaborated in the contract document, in order to comply with the Project's objective.

6. The National Recovery Program Bureau (NRPB) now invites eligible firms (“Consultant”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultant should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

a. General Experience

Minimum 10 years of experience in land development, infrastructure planning, engineering design, or similar multidisciplinary consultancy services.

b. Specific Experience

Demonstrated successful completion, within the last ten (10) years, of at least three (3) assignments of a similar nature involving one or more of the following:

i. land development planning and master planning;

ii. geotechnical investigations and site assessments;

iii. engineering design for infrastructure and utilities;

iv. preparation of procurement documentation for civil works;

v. construction supervision of civil engineering works.

c. Technical Capacity

Demonstrated capability to mobilize a multidisciplinary team covering, at a minimum:

Civil Engineering / Infrastructure Design;

Geotechnical Engineering;

Environmental and Social (ESHS);

Surveying / GIS / CAD;

Construction Supervision;

Procurement / Contract Administration.

CVs are not requested at the EOI stage - Key experts shall be requested only after the most qualified firm is invited to submit its technical and financial proposal.

d. Regional Experience (Desirable)

Experience in Small Island Developing States (SIDS), the Caribbean region, or projects with comparable environmental and operational conditions will be considered an

advantage.

e. Development Partner Experience (Desirable)

Experience on projects financed by the World Bank or other international financial institutions (IFIs) will be considered an advantage.

7. The selection process will be undertaken in line with the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Fourth Edition November 2020 (“Procurement Regulations”) for open competitive selection. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant Qualification Selection method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

8. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” (November 2020) (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

9. All submissions should be uploaded via the NRPB’s procurement portal which can be done via: National Recovery Program Bureau of St. Maarten - Consulting Services for Land Survey and Planning no later than Monday, August 10th, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. Atlantic Standard Time.

10. All queries from interested bidders must be submitted electronically to https://nrpbsxm.bonfirehub.com through the Vendor Discussions section under the respective Project (procurement) https://nrpbsxm.bonfirehub.com/portal/?tab=pastOpportunities Interested bidders should register in the NRPB's procurement portal at https://nrpbsxm.bonfirehub.com/login/. Detailed instructions for registration are available at https://nrpbsxm.org/procurement/ (NRPB EUNA SOLUTIONS REGISTRATION PAGE).

11. Once registered, bidders will have access to the relevant information, may submit questions, and respond to the procurement opportunity.

Sous l’autorité du Coordonnateur du PFCIGL, Le (a) charge (e) des opérations pour le projet aura pour mission principale d’appuyer le Coordonnateur du projet dans la supervision des opérations liées aux composantes techniques du projet.

L’Unité de Gestion du Projet de Facilitation du Commerce et Intégration dans la région des Grands Lacs, invite les consultants éligibles et répondant aux qualifications requises, à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services décrits ci-dessus.   • Être détenteur d’un diplôme universitaire d’au moins BAC+5 dans les domaines d’économie/gestion, finance, administration des affaires, sciences sociales, droit ou équivalent ou d’ingéniorat BTP.   • Justifier d'une expérience professionnelle d'au moins 10 (ans) ans en qualité d’expert dans un/des projet(s) complexe (s) financé(s) par les bailleurs de fonds internationaux, notamment la Banque mondiale (Atout majeur), en connaitre les procédures fiduciaires et de sauvegardes sociales et environnementales ;
  • Avoir une expérience dans le suivi et la supervision de l'exécution des activités dans des projets de développement/firmes d’audit/cabinets conseils ou entreprises, l’exploitation des rapports d’avancement des travaux et l’élaboration des tableaux de bord ;
  • Avoir une bonne connaissance des enjeux économiques modernes et de l’intégration économique, des associations et regroupements de défense d’intérêt dans des pays fragiles ou des pays en contexte de conflits
  • Avoir un forte capacité d’analyse, de synthèse, de rédaction et de gestion des équipes ;

MINISTRY OF TOURISM

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION)

Country: Commonwealth of Dominica

Project: Preparation Grant for Caribbean Connectivity and Logistics Regional Program – Multiphase Programmatic Approach (MPA)  

Grant No.: E5950-001

Assignment Title: Analytical Study to Support the Preparation of the Connectivity and Logistics Program for the Commonwealth of Dominica

Reference No.: DM-CSU-564635-CS-INDV

 

The Government of the Commonwealth of Dominica has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Preparation Grant for Caribbean Connectivity and Logistics Regional Program – Multiphase Programmatic Approach and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for “Analytical Study to Support the Preparation of the Connectivity and Logistics Program for the Commonwealth of Dominica”.

The Ministry of Tourism now invites eligible Individual Consultants ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

Scope of the Assignment

The Individual Consultant will be responsible for, but not limited to, the following:

  1. Conduct a focused diagnostic of Dominica's connectivity and logistics sector, including ports, road connectivity, trade facilitation, private sector participation, and green logistics.
  2. Identify priority policy reforms, institutional strengthening measures, and infrastructure investments to improve the country's transport and logistics systems.
  3. Prepare a comprehensive Dominica Country Program Document aligned with the three components of the Caribbean Reconnect Multi-Phase Programmatic Approach (MPA).
  4. Develop an implementation and financing roadmap, including investment priorities, results framework, project preparation activities, and recommendations for World Bank, IFC, and MIGA engagement.
  5. Consult with relevant government agencies, development partners, and private sector stakeholders, and facilitate a validation workshop to finalize the proposed program.

A detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment is attached to this Request for Expressions of Interest.

Minimum Qualifications and Experience

The selected consultant should possess the following:

  • A postgraduate degree in transport economics, logistics, infrastructure planning, engineering, public policy, economics, or a related field.
  • At least 12 years of professional experience in transport sector development, logistics, trade facilitation, and/or connectivity, with a strong track record in analytical and program preparation assignments.
  • Demonstrated experience in preparing World Bank-financed operations or similar assignments for multilateral development banks, including strategic program development and investment planning.
  • Proven knowledge of maritime transport, port operations, multimodal logistics, and transport sector policy and institutional frameworks.
  • Familiarity with private sector participation frameworks, climate-resilient infrastructure, and green logistics initiatives in the transport sector.
  • Experience working in Small Island Developing States (SIDS) and/or the Caribbean region will be an advantage.
  • Excellent analytical, report-writing, and communication skills, with fluency in written and spoken English.

Selection Method

The selection will be conducted in accordance with the Open International Market Approach for Individual Consultants as set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Project Financing, Goods, Works, Non-Consulting Services and Consulting Services (February 2025), and is open to all eligible consultants as defined in the Procurement Regulations.

Interested consultants should note the provisions on Conflict of Interest as set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations.

Submission of Expressions of Interest

Interested Individual Consultants should submit an Expression of Interest comprising:

  • A cover letter expressing interest in the assignment;
  • A detailed Curriculum Vitae (CV) demonstrating relevant qualifications and experience; and
  • Any other supporting documentation relevant to the assignment.

Expressions of Interest must be submitted by Monday, August 17, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. (local time) by email or in hard copy to the address below.

 

Attention:

Ms. Carolla Belle

Deputy General Manager
Dominica Air & Sea Ports Authority  
Woodbridge Bay, Fond Cole, P.O. Box 243,

Roseau, Commonwealth of Dominica

Telephone: 767-255-9110 | 767-266-3158
Email: deputygm@daspa.dm with a copy to crlcprocurement@gmail.com
Website: https://www.domports.daspa.dm

Late submissions may not be considered. Only shortlisted consultants will be contacted.

 

 

 

GOVERNMENT OF THE COMMONWEALTH OF DOMINICA

MINISTRY OF TOURISM

 

TERMS OF REFERENCE

Project ID: 

P182034

Project Name: 

Caribbean Connectivity and Logistics Regional Program – Multiphase Programmatic Approach (MPA)  

Procurement Category:

Consultancy Services

Selection Type:

Individual Consultant (IC)

Assignment Title:

Analytical Study to Support the Preparation of the Connectivity and Logistics Program for the Commonwealth of Dominica.

Duration of Assignment:

Six (6) Months

Estimated Start Date:

September 01, 2026

 

1. Background and Context

The Commonwealth of Dominica is a small island developing state (SIDS) in the Eastern Caribbean, with a population of approximately 72,000 and an economy heavily dependent on tourism, agriculture, and remittances. Like many OECS member states, Dominica faces structural connectivity challenges that constrain trade competitiveness, private sector growth, and economic resilience. Its main trade gateway — the Port of Roseau — suffers from infrastructure limitations, including a cargo pier design that restricts operational efficiency due to warehouses occupying a significant portion of the terminal, and the absence of ship-to-shore equipment. The Port of Portsmouth serves as a dedicated cargo terminal but is also constrained in capacity. Road connectivity, particularly to rural and agricultural areas, remains inadequate and highly vulnerable to natural disasters.

Dominica is also highly exposed to climate-related shocks. Hurricane Maria (2017) caused damages estimated at over 220 percent of GDP, severely disrupting transport infrastructure, supply chains, and livelihoods. This experience has underscored the urgent need to build not only more efficient but fundamentally more resilient connectivity infrastructure and logistics systems.

The Caribbean Reconnect Multi-Phase Programmatic Approach (MPA) is a joint World Bank Group initiative — involving the World Bank, IFC, and MIGA — designed to strengthen connectivity, logistics, and infrastructure across the Caribbean. The program is structured around the following three components:

  • Component 1 (Reforms), which establishes enabling regulatory foundations at national and regional levels with a focus on Private Sector Participation (PSP), trade facilitation, and supply chain security;
  • Component 2 (Enabling Infrastructure), which identifies and prepares high-impact national infrastructure investments including port modernization, resilient connectivity, digitalization, and decarbonization; and
  • Component 3 (Mobilization), which develops a regional financing scheme to aggregate projects and unlock private capital at scale.

Phase 1 of the program is expected by FY2028, with the Eastern Caribbean Corridor as the first movers.

This Terms of Reference (ToR) concerns the preparation of the Dominica country program under the Caribbean Reconnect MPA. The Consultant's primary task is to produce the analytical and strategic foundation needed to design a coherent Dominica program across all three MPA components, calibrated to Dominica's market status and grounded in the government's own priorities.

A critical and distinctive feature of this assignment is that the Government of Dominica, through DASPA, has already developed a substantive project concept — the DASPA Digitalization Project Conceptualization Proposal — covering a structured six-component digital transformation roadmap for DASPA's port operations. The Government-owned concept represents a significant investment of institutional knowledge and strategic thinking, and must be treated as the primary analytical foundation for the digitalization and infrastructure dimensions of the program. The technical review and validation of this concept will be carried out in parallel by World Bank STCs with specialized port technology expertise. The Consultant under this ToR will ensure that the findings of that review are fully integrated into the Dominica program design.

2. Objectives of the Assignment

The consultancy has two (2) overarching objectives:

  • Objective 1 — Connectivity and Logistics Diagnostic: To produce a focused, evidence-based diagnostic of Dominica's connectivity and logistics landscape — covering maritime port infrastructure, road connectivity and hinterland access, inter-island maritime services, trade facilitation, private sector participation readiness, and green logistics opportunities — identifying the key constraints and opportunities that the Reconnect MPA country program should address. The diagnostic must be structured to generate findings that directly inform the design of all three MPA components (Reforms, Enabling Infrastructure, Mobilization).
  • Objective 2 — Dominica MPA Country Program Design: To produce a structured, financeable Dominica Country Program Document, aligned with the three-component architecture of the Caribbean Reconnect MPA, that integrates: (a) the findings of the World Bank STC technical review of the DASPA Digitalization Concept; (b) the broader connectivity and logistics diagnostic; and (c) an assessment of private sector participation opportunities and the joint WBG engagement strategy (World Bank, IFC, MIGA). The Country Program Document must be sufficiently developed to serve as the basis for a World Bank lending operation under the Reconnect MPA, with a target of FY2028 for Phase 1.

3. Scope of Work

3.1 Component 1: Focused Connectivity and Logistics Diagnostic

To complement the government's digitalization concept with the broader analytical framing required by the Caribbean Reconnect Program, the Consultant will conduct a targeted — not exhaustive — diagnostic of Dominica's connectivity and logistics landscape. Given the budget and duration of this assignment, the diagnostic should be focused and evidence-based, drawing heavily on existing data and studies rather than generating new primary research from scratch. The diagnostic will cover the following dimensions:

  • Port infrastructure and operations: A focused assessment of the Port of Roseau (Woodbridge Bay) and the Port of Portsmouth (Longhouse), covering physical infrastructure, equipment gaps, cargo dwell times, throughput trends, operational bottlenecks, the cruise-cargo interface challenge at Roseau, and resilience to natural hazards, with a view to identify a priority investment program, in particular for Woodbridge Bay, to improve and rationalize operations in the short-term. Where relevant, the assessment should also consider the implications of Dominica's planned new cargo port for the future configuration of port operations.  To this end, the diagnosis shall include comprehensive Terms of Reference for the drafting of a National Port Development Master Plan.

 

  • Road connectivity and hinterland access: An assessment of the road network linking ports to key productive zones (particularly agricultural areas and agro-processing facilities), population centers, and inter-island ferry terminals. The analysis should focus on: identifying the most critical road links for logistics efficiency; assessing vulnerability to natural disasters and climate events; and estimating the logistics cost implications of road quality and reliability constraints. This analysis should draw on existing road assessments and post-Maria reconstruction data rather than generating new surveys.

 

  • Inter-island maritime connectivity: A review of current maritime services connecting Dominica to its neighbors (particularly Guadeloupe, Martinique, and other OECS islands), covering frequency, reliability, cargo capacity, and freight rates. The assessment should identify specific constraints — such as port infrastructure limitations, regulatory barriers, or limited-service competition — that restrict Dominica's ability to trade efficiently within the region, and assess opportunities for improving inter-island maritime services as part of the rEconnect program.

 

  • Trade facilitation and customs: A review of existing customs procedures, border management systems, and compliance status with the WTO Trade Facilitation Agreement, identifying key regulatory and procedural barriers affecting importers, exporters, and logistics service providers.

 

  • Trade flows and private sector landscape: A concise review of Dominica's import/export patterns, trade costs, and key private sector logistics actors (freight forwarders, shipping agents, trucking companies, warehouse operators), drawing on available data from Customs, DASPA, and regional sources. The analysis should assess how logistics costs and connectivity constraints affect the competitiveness of Dominica's key productive sectors, particularly agriculture and agro-processing.

 

  • Institutional and regulatory framework: An assessment of the mandates, capacity, and coordination mechanisms of DASPA, Customs and Excise Division, the Ministry of Public Works (for roads), the Ministry of Finance, and other relevant agencies. This should identify key institutional gaps, overlaps, and coordination failures that the program should address, as well as the regulatory framework governing maritime services and road transport.

Beyond the above dimensions, the diagnostic must also address two cross-cutting themes that are central to the Reconnect MPA:

  1. Private Sector Participation (PSP) Readiness: An assessment of the current state and potential for private sector participation in Dominica's port and logistics sector. This should cover: existing concession or PPP arrangements (if any); the regulatory and institutional framework governing PSP; private sector interest and capacity; and the specific barriers — legal, institutional, financial, reputational — that constrain private sector engagement. Given Dominica's classification as a less-mature market, the assessment should identify the foundational reforms and institutional strengthening measures needed to create conditions for PSP over the medium term, as well as any near-term opportunities that IFC or MIGA could support.
  2. Green Logistics and Decarbonization: A high-level baseline assessment of the carbon footprint and energy intensity of Dominica's port and logistics operations, and an identification of priority opportunities for decarbonization — such as shore power, solar energy for port facilities, fuel-efficient vessels for inter-island services, or green logistics zone design. This should inform the inclusion of decarbonization investments in the infrastructure component of the program.

The diagnostic should yield a concise, structured synthesis of findings organized around the three MPA components — Reforms, Enabling Infrastructure, and Mobilization — clearly identifying what the Dominica program should address under each component.

3.2 Component 2: Dominica MPA Country Program Document

Drawing on the Connectivity and Logistics Diagnostic (Component 1) and the World Bank STC technical review of the DASPA Digitalization Concept, the Consultant will produce a Dominica MPA Country Program Document. This is the primary output of the assignment. It must be structured explicitly around the three components of the Caribbean Reconnect MPA, and must be sufficiently detailed to serve as the basis for a World Bank lending operation targeting FY2028.

The document will cover:

  • MPA Component 1 — Reforms (National and Regional Level): Based on the institutional and regulatory diagnostic, the Consultant will design a reform agenda for Dominica covering: (a) the regulatory and governance framework for port operations and maritime services, including any changes needed to enable PSP; (b) trade facilitation and supply chain security reforms, including progress toward WTO TFA compliance and integration with regional single-window and harmonization initiatives; and (c) any regional-level regulatory commitments (e.g., OECS harmonization) that Dominica should advance as part of the MPA. For each reform area, the document should specify the reform action, the responsible agency, the expected timeline, and the technical assistance or capacity building support needed from the program.

 

  • MPA Component 2 — Enabling Infrastructure (National Level): Based on the diagnostic and the DASPA Digitalization Concept (as defined by the World Bank STC review), the Consultant will design an infrastructure investment program for Dominica covering: (a) port digitalization, structured around the government's six-component DASPA concept as technically validated by the STC review, with its own investment envelope, procurement modality, and results indicators; (b) complementary port physical infrastructure investments (where gaps are identified beyond what the digitalization program addresses), this shall include in particular priority short-term investments in Woodbridge Bay, complemented with the ToRs for a National Port Development Master Plan; (c) priority road connectivity investments linking ports to productive zones and inter-island ferry terminals; (d) inter-island maritime infrastructure (jetties, terminals, safety systems) where warranted; and (e) decarbonization investments in port and logistics operations. For each investment, the document should include an order-of-magnitude cost estimate, a proposed financing modality, and a readiness assessment.

 

  • MPA Component 3 — Mobilization: Based on the PSP readiness assessment, the Consultant will outline Dominica's positioning within the regional mobilization strategy of the Reconnect MPA. This section should: identify the foundational steps needed before private capital can be attracted at scale; propose a sequenced PSP roadmap for the medium term; identify any specific near-term opportunities for IFC engagement (e.g., advisory support for a port concession framework) or MIGA political risk coverage; and assess how Dominica's program can be aggregated with other Eastern Caribbean countries to form a viable regional investment corridor.

Cross-cutting Elements: In addition to the three component-specific sections, the document will:

  • Define the program's overall development objective, theory of change, results framework, and key performance indicators — structured to reflect outcomes across all three MPA components.
  • Propose a financing strategy that combines World Bank IDA resources, climate finance instruments (given Dominica's vulnerability and the decarbonization agenda), and potential IFC/MIGA engagement, taking into account Dominica's fiscal constraints and debt situation.
  • Provide a project preparation roadmap covering: environmental and social assessment requirements; procurement planning; institutional implementation arrangements (including the role of the CSU/PIU); and the sequencing of steps needed to reach project appraisal by the FY2028 target.
  • Incorporate lessons from comparable Caribbean and SIDS programs. Aviation-related comparators are not required.

Validation Workshop: Before finalizing the Country Program Document, the Consultant will organize and facilitate a validation workshop with relevant government decision-makers and key stakeholders. The workshop will present the proposed program scope, investment priorities, reform agenda, and implementation roadmap across all three MPA components, and will seek formal endorsement of the program direction from senior government counterparts. The workshop should be held in Dominica and timed to take place after the submission of the Draft Country Program Document (D3) and before the final version (D4), so that validation feedback can be incorporated into the final document. A brief workshop report summarizing discussions, decisions, and any agreed amendments to the program scope should be submitted alongside D4. The World Bank Task Team will co-facilitate the workshop alongside the Consultant.

5. Methodology and Approach

Given the budget and duration of this assignment, the Consultant is expected to adopt a focused, evidence-based methodology that maximizes the use of existing analytical work — particularly the DASPA Digitalization Conceptualization Proposal and the As-Is Business Process Analysis — rather than duplicating prior efforts. Key methodological requirements include:

  • Government Concept as the Anchor: The DASPA Digitalization Project Conceptualization Proposal must be the starting point and primary reference document for the entire assignment. The Consultant is expected to engage closely with DASPA from the outset to understand the government's vision and ensure the work is fully aligned with it. While the technical review of the digitalization concept is handled by World Bank STCs, the Consultant must engage with that parallel process, track its outputs, and ensure they are seamlessly integrated into the Program Framework Document.

 

  • Desk Review: Comprehensive review of the DASPA Digitalization Conceptualization Proposal, the As-Is Business Process Analysis outputs (as they become available), national development plans, World Bank analytical work on Dominica and the Caribbean, and relevant regional studies.

 

  • Stakeholder Consultations: Structured interviews with key government agencies (DASPA, Customs and Excise Division, Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Trade) and selected private sector actors. The Consultant is expected to participate in at least one multi-stakeholder validation workshop in Dominica.

 

  • In-Country Mission: At least one in-country mission (minimum ten working days) covering on-site visits to the Port of Roseau and Port of Portsmouth, assessment of key road corridors linking ports to productive zones, meetings with inter-island maritime service operators, and meetings with all key government and private sector counterparts. Aviation facilities and authorities are not part of the in-country mission scope.

 

  • Climate and Disaster Resilience Lens: All design and diagnostic work must integrate climate and disaster risk considerations, consistent with World Bank climate screening requirements.

 

  • Regional Coherence: Findings and recommendations must be consistent with the Caribbean Reconnect Program framework and compatible with regional digital and logistics standards being developed across participating countries.

 

6. Required Qualifications and Experience

The assignment will be undertaken by an Individual Consultant with demonstrated expertise in transport economics, logistics, and connectivity planning. The Consultant should possess the following qualifications and experience:

Senior Transport and Logistics Economist / Connectivity Specialist

Minimum Qualifications and Experience

  • A postgraduate degree in transport economics, economics, logistics, infrastructure planning, engineering, public policy, or a related discipline.
  • At least 12 years of professional experience in transport sector development, logistics, trade facilitation, and/or connectivity, with a strong track record in analytical and program preparation assignments.
  • Demonstrated experience preparing World Bank lending operations or equivalent multilateral programs, including familiarity with results frameworks, theory of change, investment program design, financing strategies, and project preparation roadmaps.
  • Solid understanding of the broader transport and logistics sector — encompassing maritime port operations, road connectivity, inter-island shipping, and trade facilitation — sufficient to produce a credible multimodal connectivity diagnostic and to integrate the outputs of the World Bank STC review of the DASPA Digitalization Concept into a coherent program. Aviation expertise is not required.
  • Familiarity with private sector participation frameworks in the port and logistics sector, including PPP structuring, concession frameworks, and the roles of IFC and MIGA in supporting private investment in infrastructure.
  • Familiarity with green logistics and decarbonization concepts in the port and transport sector, sufficient to identify investment opportunities and integrate them into a program design.
  • Previous experience working in Small Island Developing States (SIDS) or the Caribbean region is strongly preferred. Knowledge of the OECS institutional and regulatory environment is an advantage.
  • Familiarity with climate-resilient infrastructure design and disaster risk management in the transport sector.
  • Excellent written and spoken English; strong analytical writing and communication skills.

7.0 Level of Effort

The estimated level of effort of the assignment is approximately 90–100 working days over a six-month period.

The Consultant may propose to engage a local Dominica-based facilitator for in-country stakeholder consultations, within the overall budget envelope.

8.0 Reporting and Governance

The Consultant will report to the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Tourism, who will serve as the primary government counterpart. The Consultant will work in close collaboration with the Dominica Air and Sea Ports Authority (DASPA). The World Bank Task Team will provide technical oversight and review all deliverables.

9.0 Budget, Timing, Duration, and Logistics

The estimated budget available for this assignment is up to USD 110,000, inclusive of all professional fees, travel, accommodation, subsistence, withholding tax in accordance with the laws of the Commonwealth of Dominica, and any other costs required to complete the assignment. The contract will be negotiated with the selected Individual Consultant and will be implemented on a lump sum basis, with payments made against the satisfactory completion and acceptance of the agreed deliverables.

The consultancy is expected to commence in September 2026 and will be completed over a period of six (6) months. The estimated level of effort required from the Individual Consultant is approximately 90–100 working days. This estimate is provided for planning purposes only and does not constitute a basis for payment, which will be made against accepted deliverables.

The Consultant will be responsible for arranging and financing all travel, accommodation, and logistics required for in-country missions within the agreed lump sum amount. The Government of Dominica, through DASPA, the Ministry responsible for Ports, the Ministry responsible for Infrastructure, and the Ministry of Finance, will facilitate access to relevant government counterparts, available data and studies (including the DASPA Digitalization Conceptualization Proposal), and relevant stakeholder networks required for successful completion of the assignment.

9.0 Confidentiality and Ownership of Information

All data, analysis, and reports produced under this assignment are the property of the Government of Dominica. The Consultant shall treat all information obtained during the assignment as strictly confidential and shall not disclose it to any third party without the prior written consent of the Government. The Consultant shall declare any conflict of interest prior to commencement and throughout the assignment.

procnotices.bid_description: Recrutement d’un consultant individuel/assistant technique pour appuyer à l’élaboration du programme national de modernisation des villes au Cameroun
procnotices.contact_address: B.P 615 YAOUNDE
procnotices.contact_organization: MINISTERE DE L'HABITAT ET DU DEVELOPPEMENT URBAIN
procnotices.notice_text:
APPEL A MANIFESTATION D’INTERET (AMI)

N°0101/E/2/AMI/MINHDU/SG/UGP-PVGFD/RDU/RPM/2026, DU 17/07/2026

Pays :                      Cameroun

Projet :                     Projet Villes et Gestion Foncière Durable (PVGFD)

Financement :          Crédits IDA-7793-CM et IDA-7794-CM

Titre de la mission :   Recrutement d’un consultant individuel/Assistant technique pour appuyer à l’élaboration du programme national de modernisation des villes au Cameroun

N° de référence :      CM-MINHDU-559773-CS-INDV du Plan de Passation de Marchés approuvé par la Banque Mondiale du 03/07/2026

  1. Le Gouvernement de la République du Cameroun a obtenu un financement de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA), pour couvrir le coût du Projet Villes et Gestion Foncière Durable (PVGFD) et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce financement pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat de Consultant individuel/assistant technique pour appuyer à l’élaboration du programme national de modernisation des villes au Cameroun
  2. L'objectif global de cette consultation est de recruter un assistant technique pour accompagner le Secrétariat Technique et le Comité interministériel dans la conduite et l’aboutissement du processus d’élaboration du Programme National de Modernisation des Villes au Cameroun, conformément à la Feuille de route approuvée à cet effet. L’Assistant Technique interviendra en appui au Secrétariat Technique, qui demeure l’instance responsable de la conduite technique du processus de formulation du programme. Son rôle consistera principalement à fournir l’assistance méthodologique, analytique et organisationnelle nécessaire à la bonne exécution des travaux, à faciliter la coordination des contributions des différentes parties prenantes et à contribuer à la qualité technique ainsi qu’au caractère opérationnel des livrables produits dans le cadre du processus
  3. Spécifiquement, dans ce cadre, son action consistera notamment à :
      • Appuyer le Secrétariat Technique dans la planification, l’organisation, la coordination et le suivi du processus de formulation du PNMV, conformément à la Feuille de route approuvée ;
      • Contribuer à la structuration méthodologique des travaux ainsi qu’à l’élaboration des TDRs, outils, canevas et méthodes nécessaires à leur mise en œuvre ;
      • Accompagner le Secrétariat Technique dans la collecte, l’analyse, la consolidation et la mise en cohérence des informations, données et contributions techniques nécessaires à la formulation du programme ;
      • Appuyer la réalisation des diagnostics et analyses techniques, économiques, institutionnelles, territoriales, sociales et environnementales requis, ainsi que l’identification des principaux enjeux, contraintes et opportunités de développement des villes concernées ;
      • Appuyer l’organisation, l’animation, la documentation et la consolidation des résultats des consultations, concertations et ateliers organisés dans le cadre du processus ;
      • Accompagner le Secrétariat Technique dans l’identification, la priorisation et la structuration des investissements, réformes et actions stratégiques du PNMV ;
      • Fournir un appui-conseil au Secrétariat Technique et au Comité interministériel sur les aspects institutionnels, opérationnels, économiques, financiers et stratégiques liés à la formulation et à la mise en œuvre du programme, en s’appuyant notamment sur les expériences et bonnes pratiques pertinentes ;
      • Accompagner le Secrétariat Technique dans la traduction des orientations retenues en un programme opérationnel et réaliste, incluant les modalités de mise en œuvre, les mécanismes de financement, le dispositif de suivi-évaluation ainsi que la consolidation progressive des différents livrables du PNMV ;
      • Assurer toute autre tâche d’appui technique qui pourrait lui être confiée par le Secrétariat Technique dans le cadre du processus de formulation du PNMV.

Les Termes de Référence détaillés pour la mission peuvent être obtenus à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessous.

  1. La consultation est à temps plein et sera exécutée sur une période de sept (7) mois. L’échéancier prévisionnel de réalisation de cette mission est détaillé dans la feuille de Route.
  1. Le Ministre de l’Habitat et du Développement Urbain, invite les firmes de consultants (ci-après désignés Consultants) à manifester leur intérêt pour la réalisation des présentes prestations. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l’exécution desdites prestations (brochures, description de missions semblables, expérience dans des conditions similaires, disponibilité des compétences parmi le personnel, …).

N.B. : Bien vouloir justifier par les pages de garde et de signature du contrat, ainsi que les attestations de bonne fin ou tout autre document attestant que le contrat a été exécuté dans de bonnes conditions. Aussi, il est demandé de produire une liste détaillée des références, faisant ressortir pour chacune, L'intitulé de la mission, l'année de réalisation, les dates de début et de fin de mission, Le montant des prestations et le commanditaire.

Les critères de présélection sont les suivants :

Il est prévu que la présente mission soit réalisée par un consultant individuel disposant d’un profil senior, justifiant des qualifications et de l’expérience minimales requises ci-après :

Formation et expérience générale

  • Diplôme universitaire minimum de Bac + 5 dans les domaines de l’urbanisme, de la gestion des villes, de l’aménagement du territoire, de l’ingénierie civile ou urbaine, ou disciplines connexes ;
  • Au moins 10 ans d’expérience professionnelle dans la gestion de projets urbains, la planification urbaine et le développement territorial, de préférence dans des programmes nationaux ou internationaux ;

Adéquation avec la mission

  • Justifier des références dans les domaines de la planification/ gestion urbaine et/ou la formulation de programme de développement en milieu urbain, dont au moins une (01) étude/ projet similaire en qualité de Chef de Mission ou Chef de projet au cours des dix (10) dernières années, de préférence en Afrique Sub-saharienne ;
  • Justifier d’une expérience dans la formulation de programmes, stratégies ou plans d’investissement de développement urbain ou territorial d’envergure similaire, incluant la définition des orientations stratégiques, la priorisation des actions, les modalités de mise en œuvre et les mécanismes de suivi-évaluation ;
  • Justifier d’une expérience avérée dans l’analyse économique urbaine, la conduite d’études d’impact économique, et la priorisation des investissements de développement ;
  • Justifier d’une bonne connaissance et/ou expérience en finances urbaines ou municipales, incluant les mécanismes de financement, les stratégies de mobilisation des ressources ou les cadres de financement des programmes.
  • Justifier d’une expertise en coordination dans un contexte multipartite et dans la conduite d'entretiens, d'ateliers participatifs avec les communautés et les acteurs locaux, ainsi qu’une bonne capacité à analyser les aspects institutionnels et les cadres réglementaires locaux ;

Atouts

  • Une expérience professionnelle de quinze (15) ans ou plus constituera un atout, notamment pour les candidats ayant une expérience avérée dans la conduite de programmes nationaux ou de réformes sectorielles ;
  • Avoir une bonne expérience de l’Afrique subsaharienne et une bonne connaissance du contexte institutionnel, socio-économique et environnemental du Cameroun ;
  • Avoir une bonne maitrise du français et une bonne connaissance de l’anglais, ou vice-versa (oral et écrit) ;
  • Avoir une expérience dans le cadre de projets financés par la Banque mondiale ou d’autres partenaires techniques et financiers.
  1. Il est porté à l'attention des consultants que les dispositions des paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 de la Section III du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement des Projets d'Investissement (FPI) de la Banque mondiale, édition de septembre 2025 (« Règlement de Passation des Marchés relatifs aux règles de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflit d'intérêt et d’avantages compétitifs inéquitable ») sont applicables et sont disponibles sur le site web de la Banque à l’adresse : www.worldbank.org.
  1. De plus, le Consultant sera sélectionné selon la méthode de Sélection des Consultants Individuel par mise en concurrence ouverte, telle que décrite dans le Règlement sus-décrit.
  1. Les Consultants intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations supplémentaires aux heures ouvrables entre 08 heures à 17 heure, heure locale et à l’adresse ci-dessous :

Unité de Gestion du Projet des Villes et Gestion Foncière Durables (PVGFD), Sis 3ème étage de l’immeuble OKCTOPUS, B.P 615, Yaoundé-Cameroun, Tél ; (237) 242 02 97 34, Rue 1.147 Frédéric Foe, quartier Hippodrome, à côté de la Délégation Régionale de l’ART Centre, E-mail : pvgfd.minhdu@gmail.com.

  1. Les dossiers de candidature, rédigés en français doivent parvenir / être déposés soit en version numérique en formats PDF & Word par courrier électronique, soit en version physique accompagné de la version numérique sur clé USB en format PDF & Word en six (06) exemplaires dont un (01) original et cinq (05) copies, à l’adresse ci-dessus, au plus tard 07/07/2026 à quinze (15) heures, heure locale. Elles doivent être transmises avec la mention :

« APPEL A MANIFESTATION D’INTERET (AMI) No0101/E/2/AMI/MINHDU/SG/UGP-PVGFD/RDU/RPM/2026, EN VUE DU RECRUTEMENT D’UN CONSULTANT INDIVIDUEL/ASSISTANT TECHNIQUE POUR APPUYER A L’ELABORATION DU PROGRAMME NATIONAL DE MODERNISATION DES VILLES AU CAMEROUN, DANS LE CADRE DU PROJET VILLES ET GESTION FONCIERE DURABLES (PVGFD). ».

Yaoundé, le 17/07/2026

Le Ministre

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

National Communications Consultant

                     (Ref. No. CS- 59)

 

Lao Statistics Bureau (LSB) is implementing a project titled “Lao PDR Strengthening the National Statistical Project (LAOSTAT II)” from 2023 to 2028. The Government of Lao PDR (GoL) has received a loan from the World Bank’s International Development Association (IDA) to improve the capacity of the Lao PDR NSS to produce and disseminate high-quality statistics in a timely manner, to enhance the use of key statistics, and in case of an Eligible Crisis or Emergency, respond promptly and effectively to it. The project is closely aligned with Vision 2030 and the Strategy of the Development of National Statistical System (SDNSS - 2016 – 2025) which outlines key strategies for sustained development of the Lao Statistical System (LSS). The project focuses on four components, namely (i) Improving the availability and quality of official statistics, (ii) Enhancing the use of statistics in the GoL, (iii) Strengthening institutional capacity and project management, and (iv) Contingent Emergency Response.

The LAOSTAT-II project supports National Communications Consultant to assist LAOSTAT II including the Project Director and Project Manager, in coordinating, communicating, and managing the project activities.

The Lao Statistics Bureau (LSB) is seeking a national consultant to Developing and Executing the Dissemination Plan, Coordinating Publication Schedules, Developing Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), Preparing and Leading the Web Platform Development, Planning and Leading social media and PR Efforts, Stakeholder Communication and implement systems to track the effectiveness of communication strategies.

This assignment is time-based, full-time basis with estimated service duration of 12-months starting from August 2026 to July 2027. The full ToR for the assignment can be sent to candidates upon written request to the e-mail address below.

The LAOSTAT-II Project now invites eligible individual consultants to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultant should provide information (CV, Expression of Interest, other supporting information, if any) demonstrating that s/he has the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. In order to qualify for this position, the candidates shall meet the following experience and competence requirements:

  1.  At least a university degree, preferably master’s degree, in communications, PR, journalism, marketing, digital media or a related filed. Equivalent work experience for more than 10 years may be considered in lieu of a degree. At least seven years of experience in working with website building and social media.
  2. Prior work experience in Lao PDR - ideally with government agencies and/or international organizations.
  3. Demonstrated knowledge and professional experience in project management and development planning.
  4. Fluency in written and spoken English and Lao; knowledge of other regional languages is a plus.
  5. Excellent coordination, networking, and stakeholder management skills.
  6. Advanced proficiency in standard office software packages, including word processing, and presentation software.
  7. Proven ability to apply required depth and breadth of knowledge and expertise to meet job demands.
  8. Strong planning and prioritization skills to meet the project development objectives and organizational goals.
  9. Demonstrated experience in developing and implementing successful communication strategies for complex projects or organizations.
  10. Ability to work effectively in a multicultural environment and maintain high standards of personal and professional integrity.
  11. Experience with data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI) and statistical communication is highly desirable.
  12. Professional certification in project management (e.g., PMP, PRINCE2) is preferred.
  13. The attention of interested consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016, revised November 2017 and August 2018 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by e-mail) by 08 August 2026, 16:00 Lao time (submissions via email are also acceptable). Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

procnotices.notice_text:
AVIS A MANIFESTATION D’INTERET N° 2026-005/MTDPCE/SG/DMP DU 24/07/2026 RELATIF AU RECRUTEMENT D’UNE ONG/OSC SPECIALISEE DANS LA LUTTE CONTRE LES EXPLOITATIONS ET ABUS SEXUELS/HARCELEMENT SEXUEL (EAS/HS) ET LA VIOLENCE BASEE SUR LE GENRE (VBG) DANS LE CADRE DE LA MISE EN ŒUVRE DU PROJET PACTDIGITAL

  1. CONTEXTE

Le Gouvernement du Burkina Faso a obtenu un crédit de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA), pour financer le Projet d’accélération de la transformation digitale du Burkina Faso (PACTDIGITAL) et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce crédit pour effectuer des paiements au titre du contrat suivant : Recrutement d’une ONG/OSC spécialisée dans la lutte contre les exploitations et abus sexuels/harcèlement sexuel (EAS/HS) et la violence basée sur le genre (VBG) dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre du projet PACTDIGITAL.

  1. OBJECTIF DE LA MISSION

L’objectif général de ce travail consiste à appuyer le Projet d’accélération de la transformation digitale (PACTDIGITAL) dans la prévention, atténuation des risques, et réponse aux EAS/HS et la violence basée sur le genre (VBG), liées à sa mise en œuvre, et dans le soutien holistique aux survivant(e)s dans les zones du projet.

Les objectifs spécifiques sont les suivants :

  • Cartographier de façon régulière et à travers des consultations et approches participatives, les risques de VBG dans la zone d’intervention du projet et en particulier les risques susceptibles d’être exacerbés et potentiellement prévenus par la mise en œuvre du projet, et de proposer des mesures de prévention et d’atténuation efficaces et éthiques pour leur mise en place par les différentes parties prenantes au projet ;
  • Concevoir et mettre en œuvre des campagnes de sensibilisation et prévention de ces risques aussi bien au niveau des communautés concernées qu’auprès du personnel embauché par le projet et les structures de mise en œuvre.

Ces campagnes devront comprendre, entre autres, la sensibilisation et formation régulière du personnel et des communautés touchées par le projet sur les VBG, l’EAS et le HS, leurs causes et conséquences et les risques spécifiquement liés au projet, les services de réponse disponibles aux survivant(e)s, les standards de conduite du projet et les sanctions prévues en cas de violation, le MGP, la façon de le saisir et ses objectifs, etc. ;

  • Assurer, sur la base du consentement libre, éclairé et volontaire des survivant(e)s, leur accès à une prise en charge holistique comprenant notamment les services psychosociaux, médicaux et juridiques/judiciaires, à travers la mise en œuvre d’un protocole de réponse centré sur les survivants (e) et respectueux de leurs choix, de leur dignité, de leur sécurité et de leur confidentialité ;
  • Appuyer l’équipe de Sauvegardes environnementales et sociales (SES) au sein de l’Unité de Gestion du PACTDIGITAL dans la mise en place du MGP sensible aux EAS/HS et en particulier la saisie, la gestion et le rapportage des plaintes liées aux VBG lors de la mise en œuvre des activités (installation de pylônes, déploiement de la fibre optique, construction de data center…) du projet, conformément au système de gestion des plaintes développé et mis en place pour assurer une gestion éthique et confidentielle des plaintes EAS/HS et VBG ;
  •  Appuyer le projet dans le suivi et évaluation des activités de prévention et réponse aux VBG de façon éthique.
  1. DUREE DE LA MISSION

La durée de l’intervention du prestataire est de 12 mois renouvelable jusqu’à la date de fin du projet. Les activités de sensibilisation se poursuivront régulièrement pendant tout le cycle du projet. Cette intervention s’effectuera sous la supervision de l’UGP.

  1. Les ONG/OSC peuvent s’associer avec d’autres ONG/OSC pour renforcer leurs compétences respectives en la forme d’un groupement. En cas de groupement, tous les membres de ce groupement restent conjointement et solidairement responsables de l’exécution de la mission au cas où le groupement sera sélectionné.
  2. Les TDR détaillés de la mission peuvent être obtenus au secrétariat de la DMP/MTDPCE à l’adresse ci-dessous : 1er Etage Immeuble Armelle au projet ZACA, 01 BP 5175 Ouagadougou 01, Tél. (+226) 25 49 01 38 ou en écrivant à brahima.traore@tic.gov.bf pour solliciter lesdits TDRs.
  3. Le Directeur des Marchés Publics du Ministère de la Transition Digitale des Postes et des Communications Electroniques (DMP/MTDPCE) invite les ONG/OSC à manifester leur intérêt pour fournir les services. Les ONG/OSC intéressées devraient fournir des renseignements démontrant qu’elles possèdent les qualifications et les expériences pertinentes requises pour exécuter les services. Les dossiers de manifestation d’intérêt devront comporter notamment :
  • une lettre de manifestation d’intérêt adressée à Madame la Ministre, datée et signée ;
  • une présentation de la firme faisant ressortir ses domaines de compétence ;
  • les références de prestations pertinentes en rapport avec la mission.

NB: Les prestations similaires exécutées doivent être justifiées par les copies des pages de garde et de signature des contrats comprenant explicitement l’objet et le montant du contrat et les attestations de bonne fin ou des rapports de validation. Seules les références attestées par des pièces justificatives seront prises en compte pour l’évaluation.

En cas d’ex-aequo, le montant des expériences pertinentes justifiées sera utilisé comme critère additionnel pour le classement final des consultants.

  1. L’attention des consultants intéressés est attirée sur la section III, paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du Règlement de passation des marchés pour les emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissements (FPI) septième édition de septembre 2025, exposant la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d’intérêts.
  2. Un consultant sera sélectionné suivant la méthode de Sélection dans le Cadre d’un Budget Déterminé (SCBD) telle que décrite dans le Règlement de passation des marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le financement de projets d’investissements (FPI), septième édition de septembre 2025.
  3. Des informations supplémentaires peuvent être obtenues à l’adresse du Secrétariat de la Direction des Marchés Publics du Ministère de la Transition Digitale des Postes et des Communications Electroniques (DMP/MTDPCE), sise au 1er Etage de l’immeuble Armelle au projet ZACA, 01 BP 5175 Ouagadougou 01, Tél. (+226) 25 49 01 38, E-mail : brahima.traore@tic.gov.bf et aux jours ouvrables de 07 heures 30 mn à 12 heures 30 mn et de 13 heures à 16 heures.
  4. Les manifestations d’intérêt devront être rédigées en français, multipliées en trois (03) exemplaires dont un (01) original et deux (02) copies et déposées sous plis fermés à l’adresse ci-dessus en personne ou par courrier express au plus tard le ……juillet 2026 à 09 heures 00 mn temps universel avec la mention « réponse à la manifestation d’intérêt pour le Recrutement d’une ONG/OSC spécialisée dans la lutte contre les exploitations et abus sexuels/harcèlement sexuel (EAS/HS) et la violence basée sur le genre (VBG) dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre du projet PACTDIGITAL »

AVIS D’APPEL D’OFFRE INTERNATIONAL

(Processus d’Appel d’Offres à deux Enveloppes Sans Préqualification)

 

Maître d’Ouvrage       : Ministère de l’Urbanisme et Habitat

Référence : P 179292 Crédit IDA n° 72160-ZR

Titre du Marché         : Travaux d’aménagement et de bitumage d’un tronçon de 7,7 Km de la RN 41 à Kananga 

Référence de l’AOI     : ZR-PURUK-551383-WC-RFB

Date de publication : 31 juillet 2026

Date de clôture : 21 septembre 2026

1. Le Gouvernement de la République Démocratique du Congo a obtenu un prêt de la Banque mondiale pour financer le coût du Projet d’Urgence et de Résilience Urbaine de Kananga « PURUK » et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie des sommes accordées au titre de ce financement pour effectuer les paiements prévus au titre les marchés Travaux d’aménagement et de bitumage d’un tronçon de 7,7 Km de la RN 41 à Kananga. Pour ce marché, l’Emprunteur utilisera pour les paiements la méthode de décaissement intitulée « Paiement Direct », telle que définie dans les Directives de Décaissement de la Banque mondiale pour les Financements de Projets d’Investissements (FPI)

2. L’Unité de Gestion du Projet d’Urgence et de Résilience Urbaine de Kananga « UG- PURUK » invite, par la présente, les Soumissionnaires à présenter leurs Offres sous pli fermé, pour la réalisation de Travaux d’aménagement et de bitumage d’un tronçon de 7,7 Km de la RN 41 à Kananga pour un délai d’exécution de 12 mois (compris la période de la mobilisation). La marge de préférence n’est pas applicable.

3.       La procédure sera conduite par mise en concurrence internationale en utilisant un Appel d’Offres tel que défini dans le « Règlement de Passation de Marchés de la Banque mondiale pour les Emprunteur de FPI » Septième Edition de Septembre 2025, et ouvert à tous les Soumissionnaires de pays éligibles tels que définis dans le Règlement de Passation de Marchés.

4. Les Offres seront évaluées conformément au processus d’évaluation défini dans le dossier d’appel d’offres. Les pondérations suivantes s’appliqueront aux Critères notés (y compris les facteurs techniques et autres que le prix) soixante (60 %) et pour le coût de l’Offre : quarante pourcents (40 %).

5. Les Soumissionnaires éligibles peuvent obtenir des informations supplémentaires auprès de de l’Unité de Gestion du Projet d’Urgence et de Résilience Urbaine de Kananga « UG- PURUK », 601, Avenue du GECAMINE, Quartier Malandji, Commune de Kananga, Ville de Kananga, Province du Kasaï Central, République Démocratique du Congo (RDC), Téléphone : +213 992925752, +243 811 144 595 / +243 823 041 704, Courrier : spm.puruk.cosmos@gmail.com ; ugpuruk@gmail.com, jeanmichelmbungu@gmail.com et examiner le Dossier d’Appel d’Offres durant les heures de bureau de 9h00 à 16h00 heure locale de Kananga (TU+2).

6. Le Dossier d’Appel d’offres en français peut être acheté par tout Soumissionnaire éligible intéressé en formulant une demande écrite à l’adresse ci-dessous contre un paiement non remboursable de dollars américains cinq cents (USD 500). La méthode de paiement sera virement au compte intitulé : PURUK / MIN. FINANCES DAO, Numéro du Compte : 00011-15069-92001858517-97 USD à la Banque Equitty BCDC. Le dossier d’appel d’offres sera remis physiquement aux candidats soumissionnaires à Kananga ou envoyé par courriel don’t l’UG PURUK n’est pas responsable des aléas, après présentation de la preuve de paiement.

7. Les Soumissions doivent être remises à l’adresse ci-dessous au plus tard le 21 septembre 2026 à 14h00 heure locale de Kananga (TU+2). Le dépôt d’offres par voie électronique ne sera pas permis. Toute Soumission reçue en retard sera écartée. Les enveloppes extérieures de l’Offre marquées « ORIGINAL DE L’OFFRE », et les enveloppes intérieures marquées « PARTIE TECHNIQUE » seront ouvertes en présence des représentants des Soumissionnaires et de toute personne qui souhaitent assister à l’ouverture des plis à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessous, le 21 Septembre 2026 à 14h30 heure locale de Kananga (TU+2). Toutes les enveloppes marquées « PARTIE FINANCIERE » demeureront non-ouvertes et seront conservées dans un lieu sûr par le Maître d’Ouvrage jusqu’à la seconde ouverture publique des Offres.

8. Les Soumissions doivent être accompagnées : (i) d’une Garantie d’offre d’un montant de 250 000 USD (Dollars américains deux cents cinquante mille), (ii) d’une Déclaration relative à l’Exploitation et aux Abus Sexuels (EAS) et/ou au Harcèlement Sexuel (HS), et (iii) d’une Déclaration d’Engagement de la main d’œuvre locale.

9.     Veuillez noter que le Règlement de Passation des Marchés exige que l’Emprunteur divulgue les informations sur les propriétaires effectifs du Soumissionnaire attributaire, dans le cadre de l’avis de Notification d’Attribution de Marché, en renseignant le Formulaire de Divulgation des Bénéficiaires Effectifs inclus dans le dossier d’appel d’offres.

COUNTRY:                                       Federal Republic of Somalia

NAME OF PROJECT:                    Regional Digital Integration Project (EA-RDIP)  

PROJECT ID:                                    P176181         

Assignment Title:                          Consultancy Service for Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA)

Reference No.:                                SO-MOCT-FGS-536515-CS-CQS

Place of assignment:                   Mogadishu, Somalia

Submission Date:                         August 15, 2026, 2.00pm (local time, Mogadishu, Somalia)

The Federal Republic of Somalia has received a grant from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank toward the cost of the Regional Digital Integration Project (EA-RDIP), and the Ministry of Communications and Technology intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“Services”) is required to be undertaken as an external consultant firm supporting the client, Ministry of Communications and Technology (MoCT), FGS to carry out the implementation of “Consulting Firm to conduct Environmental and Social Impact Assessments (ESIA) and Resettlement Action Plans (RAP) for the proposed Galkayo – Hobyo Fiber Optic Corridor in Somalia”. The consultant firm will undertake all the specific required tasks detailed out in the Terms of Reference (ToR). The consultant service is expected to be conducted and reports delivered in approximately six (6) months from commencement of the contract.

Terms of Reference (ToR) can be found at the following website: https://moct.gov.so/en/jobs/ or it can be provided upon submission of application in person or by e-mail. The e-mail address is provided below.

The Ministry of Communications and Technology now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (brochures, description of similar assignments, experience in similar conditions, availability of appropriate skills among staff, etc.).  The short-listing criteria are as follows:

The short-listing criteria are as follows:

  1. Core business of the firm and years in Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) and Resettlement Action Plan (RAP) should be at least 10 years, with evidence of the company registration certificate, business license or operationalpermit, and providing company profile indicating services offered and years in operation.
  2. The firm must have a minimum of 5 years of experience in providing similar assignments in Information and Communication Technology (ICT) sector. The Consulting firm should demonstrate at least 2 similar assignments successfully implemented during the last 5 years in environmental and social risks management including the Environmental and Social Impact Assessment, and experience in with the World Bank’s Environmental and Social Safeguards (ESS1- ESS10) is required.
  3. Demonstrate experience of relevant services implemented in Somalia, or an environment similar to that of Somalia; and
